I plant maize and cassava together on this rented plot, as my father taught me and as my neighbors here do. I will buy one bag of NPK fertilizer from the agro-dealer if he comes to the village when I have cash, because the soil is tired and the maize needs it, but I will not spend money on improved seed when my own seed from last season is still good and kept in the house. My wife and children will do all the work between us — clearing, planting, weeding, harvesting — about seventy days in total over the season. I do not spray chemicals on the crops and I do not irrigate; I pull the weeds with my hands and I wait for the rains to come as they always do here.
